title: Simple interest
goal: I can calculate simple interest and the final amount.
teach: Interest is the cost of borrowing money or the reward for saving it. With simple interest the interest is the same every year: I = P × r × n, where P is the principal (amount invested), r the rate per year as a decimal and n the number of years. The final amount A = P + I.

ex.q: Find the simple interest on R4 000 at 9% per year for 6 months.
steps: 6 months = 0,5 years, so P = 4 000, r = 0,09, n = 0,5.

watch:
Write the rate as a decimal (8% = 0,08) and the time in years.

Problem-solving lens
Work out one year’s interest first; simple interest is the same every year.

qs.text: Find the simple interest on R5 000 at 6% for 2 years.
qs.steps:
1. Formula (simple interest): I = P × r × n, where P is the amount invested or borrowed, r is the yearly rate as a decimal and n is the number of years. Final amount A = P + I.
2. I = 5 000 × 0,06 × 2
3. = R600

qs.text: R1 500 is invested at 10% simple interest for 4 years. Find the final amount.
qs.steps:
1. Formula (simple interest): I = P × r × n, where P is the amount invested or borrowed, r is the yearly rate as a decimal and n is the number of years. Final amount A = P + I.
2. I = 1 500 × 0,1 × 4 = R600
3. A = R1 500 + R600 = R2 100

qs.text: Find the simple interest on R4 000 at 9% per year for 6 months.
qs.steps:
1. Formula (simple interest): I = P × r × n, where P is the amount invested or borrowed, r is the yearly rate as a decimal and n is the number of years. Final amount A = P + I.
2. 6 months = 0,5 years
3. I = 4 000 × 0,09 × 0,5 = R180
